item.p: The lack of τοῦ before Ἀ̣πίωνος makes the interpretation of the line somewhat uncertain. If the taxpayer was a son of Patron son of Apion, compare perhaps P.Mil.Vogl. III 132-133 (both from Tebtynis, 165), where a Σαβεῖνος Πάτρωνος τοῦ Ἀπίωνος appears as one of four lessees.
Musthes the elder son of Apunchis and grandson of Phombos might find a brother in P.Münch. III/1 145.26 (Tebtynis, mid-II): [Φ]ᾶσις Ἀ[πύ]γχεως τοῦ Φομ̣β̣ο͂ς μ(ητρὸς) Θεν[ηρ]α̣κλ̣ίας.

For ὥς φησιν after the name of a slave or freedman to indicate that he/she is designated through his/her most commonly used name (and maybe not the one originally given), compare BGU XV 2548.7 (Arsinoites, 117-138: Θαῆσις ὥς φησιν δο̣ύλ̣(η)); P.Coll.Youtie I 25.6 (Tebtynis, 147: Σαραπίων ὥς φησιν ἀπελεύθερος); P.Ross.Georg. II 18.xix.86 (Arsinoites, 139-140: Χαρεῖν[ος(?)] ὥς φησιν ἀπελ[εύθερος).
